prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — but “best” depends on your home, budget and priorities (price, speed, warranty, brand, energy efficiency). A few quick questions so I can recommend the right companies and give accurate estimates:

- What’s your ZIP code (or neighborhood) in Atlanta?
- Do you have central ducted AC now or mini‑splits/packaged unit?
- Rough square footage of your home and age of the current system (if any)?
- Any brand preferences or budget range?
- How soon do you need the replacement?

While you answer, here are practical steps and what to look for so you hire a quality contractor:

Checklist when choosing a company
- Get at least 3 written estimates that include: equipment model and SEER rating, scope of work, labor warranty, permits, and removal of old unit.
- Require a Manual J load calculation (right‑sizing). Contractors who skip this often oversize units.
- Confirm credentials: EPA 608 certification (for refrigerant handling), local contractor license/registration if required by your city/county, proof of insurance (liability and workers’ comp).
- Check reviews on Google, BBB, Angi/HomeAdvisor, Yelp and Nextdoor; ask for local references and recent installations you can inspect.
- Ask about manufacturer and workmanship warranties, and whether they handle permits/inspections.
- Ask about refrigerant type (R-410A vs old R-22) — replacing an R-22 system can be more expensive due to refrigerant phase‑out.
- Compare lifecycle cost, not just upfront price: higher SEER + proper installation saves more over time.
- Beware red flags: extremely low bids, cash-only, no written contract, refusing permits, pressure to buy immediately without inspection.

Brands to consider (positioning)
- Trane / Carrier: often top reliability and dealer support, mid‑to‑high cost.
- Lennox: high‑end, very efficient models.
- Rheem / Ruud: solid mid‑range balance of price and performance.
- Goodman: budget-friendly with decent warranties (value option).
Choose a reputable installer — installation quality often matters more than brand.

Names to consider (to start your shortlist)
I can find highly rated local contractors for your exact ZIP, but generally look for established Atlanta-area firms with good review histories and clear warranties. National and regional companies with Atlanta presence include franchise networks like One Hour Heating & Air, Service Experts, and ARS/Rescue Rooter, plus many well-reviewed local contractors. Send your ZIP and I’ll pull a short list of top-rated options in your area.

If you want, I can:
- Find 4–6 top-rated HVAC companies near you (with pros/cons),
- Draft an email/script and checklist you can use to request estimates,
- Explain expected price ranges for a full system replacement for your home size.

Which would you like next?
